The case was built on the time after the broadcast; the only person at the door at that hour was Sophie.

A note was added to the file: “A person seen on screen is not thereby alive at that moment; no alibi is accepted without requesting the source of the broadcast.” Suspicion against Sophie Lindner was formally lifted.
It was assumed he died during the broadcast; the footage seen by thousands of viewers became the file’s strongest witness.
The time of death remained uncertain; the alibis were left hanging.
The sponsor company was investigated; nothing turned up. Tobias Wendt started editing a new programme.
The death was closed as an accident. The last broadcast of “Night Desk” was remembered as one its host gave after he had died; no one asked why.
Sophie Lindner was arrested. The defence turned the broadcast time into an accusation instead of an alibi; the case lasted a year.

Tobias Wendt was arrested for murder. It was revealed that the last six months of “Night Desk” had been pre-recorded; the sponsor terminated the contract. Felix’s deleted sentence was published on a news site.

LIVE BROADCAST  /  SUSPICIOUS DEATH

Late-night show host Felix Hartung is found dead in his studio flat forty minutes after ending his broadcast. Thousands of viewers watched him live until 00.58. The only person at the door was his ex-girlfriend.

On 14 July 2029 at 01.42 in Friedrichshain, a man’s body was found in a top-floor studio flat at Boxhagener Hof 12. Found by: his ex-girlfriend, Sophie Lindner, who let herself in with a spare key.

Deceased: Felix Hartung (36), host of “Night Desk”, broadcast live every night from 23.00 to 01.00. A heavy blow to the head; beside him an overturned microphone stand.

Patrol note: “The broadcast ended at 00.58; thousands of viewers saw him live. Death between 00.58 and 01.42. A neighbour saw Sophie Lindner ringing the bell at the door at 00.40. The suspect is clear.”

The autopsy put the death before the broadcast. The weather record showed that the “today’s downpour” on the broadcast fell the day before; the broadcast server log showed the broadcast came from a file, not a camera. The chat session log tied the “live” message to the phone in the bar, the location record and the entrance camera put Tobias in the building, and the edit examination tied it to the deleted confession.
Seeing someone on screen does not prove they were alive at that moment: ask for the source of the footage and the recording’s metadata. A perfect alibi is the alibi most in need of questioning.
Friedrichshain and Simon-Dach-Straße — July 2029

“Night Desk” had not been live for months: the editor, Tobias Wendt, prepared recordings and Felix Hartung broadcast them as live. Before the sponsor’s audit, Felix decided to reveal everything and put the blame on his editor. On the evening of 13 July Tobias cut the confession sentence from that night’s file, went to Felix after 21.00 and killed him with the microphone stand. Then he went on to a bar; at 23.00 the file played and Felix lived on screen for two hours. When the fire set the chat alight, he wrote a message from Felix’s account in the bar.
Who is responsible for Felix Hartung’s death?
